'''Bolognese sauce 'bambi'''' is a [[Cookbook:Venison|venison]] sauce for [[Cookbook:Pasta|pasta]]. It can be made successfully with roe deer, muntjac and springbok.

==Ingredients==
*250 [[Cookbook:g|g]] (½ [[Cookbook:Pound|lb]]) [[Cookbook:Chopping|chopped]] [[Cookbook:Onion|onion]]
*250 [[Cookbook:g|g]] (½ [[Cookbook:Pound|lb]]) finely-chopped [[Cookbook:Mushroom|mushrooms]]
*2–5 cloves of finely-chopped [[Cookbook:Garlic|garlic]] 
*30 [[Cookbook:ML|ml]] (2 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]]) [[Cookbook:Olive_Oil|olive]], [[Cookbook:Corn_Oil|corn]] or [[Cookbook:Sunflower_Oil|sunflower oil]] (according to taste)
*500 [[Cookbook:g|g]] (1.1 [[Cookbook:Pound|lb]]) [[Cookbook:Mincing|minced]]/ground) stewing venison (minced lean leftovers from trimming are ideal)
*500 [[Cookbook:ML|ml]] dry hard [[Cookbook:Cider|cider]], red or white [[Cookbook:Wine|wine]], or [[Cookbook:Stock|beef stock]] (how much you will need depends on how fast it boils away)
*60 [[Cookbook:ML|ml]] (4 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]]) [[Cookbook:Tomato_Paste|tomato purée]]
*250 [[Cookbook:g|g]] (½ [[Cookbook:Pound|lb]]) finely-[[Cookbook:Grater|grated]] [[Cookbook:Carrot|carrots]]
*5 [[Cookbook:Bay_Leaf|bay leaves]]
*30 [[Cookbook:ML|ml]] (2 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]]) [[Cookbook:Herbes_de_Provence|Herbes de Provence]]
*1 [[Cookbook:Dehydrated Broth|stock cube]] (optional)
*[[Cookbook:Salt|Salt]]
*Freshly-ground [[Cookbook:Pepper|black pepper]]
*300 [[Cookbook:g|g]] (¾ [[Cookbook:Pound|lb]]) [[Cookbook:Pasta_of_Italy|penne, spaghetti]] or whatever other pasta you prefer
*[[Cookbook:Parmesan Cheese|Parmesan cheese]]

==Procedure==
#[[Cookbook:Sautéing|Sauté]] the onions, mushrooms, and garlic in the oil until well softened.
#Add the venison and stir well until it has all (more or less) changed colour.
#Add sufficient dry cider to cover, but not too deeply.
#Add the stock cube (only if you are using wine or cider), bay leaves, grated carrot, and tomato purée, and stir well.
#[[Cookbook:Simmering|Simmer]] very gently for at least 3 hours, stirring occasionally and replenishing the liquid (with more cider/wine/stock or just water) if it gets too dry. The ideal is to have the sauce with little separate liquid when it is served, but not dry enough to scorch. It may be simmered on top of the [[Cookbook:Stovetop|stove]], or in a very low [[Cookbook:Oven|oven]], or in a [[Cookbook:Slow Cooker|slow cooker]]. The sauce is edible after about 40 minutes but is infinitely better flavoured and textured after 3 or 4 hours. In a slow cooker it can be cooked for 8 hours. The flavour is even better if it is cooked, allowed to cool overnight, and reheated for 30 or 40 minutes—but, this is a council of perfection and not really necessary.
#About 30–40 minutes before serving remove the bay leaves, add the herbes de Provence, and adjust the salt (i.e. taste it and add more salt if you think it needs it).
#Just before serving, add freshly-ground black pepper.
#Serve over ''[[Cookbook:Al Dente|al dente]]'' pasta sprinkled with grated Parmesan cheese.
